### Observed differences

- **Routing out of A14 and A15 flipped completely.** Before, every observed outgoing transition of A14 and of A15 went to A23; in the later window, every such transition goes to A18. Participation is unchanged: A14 occurs in about 52 in 100 traces before and about 53 in 100 after (103 and 105 of 200), A15 in about 48 in 100 in both windows (97 and 95 of 200), and in both windows every trace contains exactly one of the two. [DIR001, DIR002, POS001, POS002, REL001, REL005]
- **The activities feeding them changed accordingly.** Before, A22 led to A15 (about 48 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) or A14 (about 52 in 100), and A33 led to A16 (about 48) or A17 (about 52); in the later window, A22 leads to A16 (about 53) or A17 (about 47), and A33 leads to A14 (about 53) or A15 (about 47). [DIR005, DIR006]
- **The exits of A16 and A17 changed target.** Before, A16 led to A17 (about 48 in 100) or A18 (about 52), and A17 led to A18 (about 48) or A16 (about 52); in the later window, the transitions into A18 are replaced by transitions into A23: A16 leads to A17 (about 53) or A23 (about 47), A17 to A23 (about 53) or A16 (about 47). [DIR003, DIR004]
- **Positions shifted only for the involved activities.** A14 and A15 moved from a mean relative event position of about 0.67 to about 0.36, and A16 and A17 from about 0.38 to about 0.65, while A18 (about 0.43 to 0.40) and A22 (about 0.64 to 0.60) moved only slightly; A16, A17, A18, A22 and A33 occur in every trace in both windows. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- **All order relations between the two groups reversed.** Before, A16 and A17 each preceded A18 and A22 in 100% of traces; in the later window, A18 and A22 each precede A16 and A17 in 100% of traces. Likewise, before, A16, A17, A18 and A22 preceded A14 and A15 in the roughly half of traces containing them; in the later window, A14 and A15 come first in those co-occurrences. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- **Event distances match a block exchange.** The gap from A22 to A23 grew from 2 events to 3, and the gap from A33 to A18 shrank from 3 to 2. [LAG001, LAG002]
- Taken together: before, the flow after A33 ran both A16 and A17 in either order, then A18, then later A22, then exactly one of A14/A15, then A23; in the later window, after A33 exactly one of A14/A15 runs, then A18, then A22, then both A16 and A17 in either order, then A23. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two segments of the flow exchanged their order: the mandatory pair A16+A17, executed together in either order, ran before directly after A33 and before A18/A22, while the exclusive choice between A14 and A15 ran between A22 and A23; in the later window, the A14-or-A15 choice runs directly after A33 and before A18, and the A16/A17 pair runs after A22 and before A23, with A18 and A22 keeping their approximate positions and A33 and A23 remaining the surrounding anchors. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL001, REL005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]

The support is direct and consistent: the order reversal between {A16, A17} and {A18, A22} is observed relationally and completely (co-occurrence stays at 100% of traces while the order flips from 100%/0% to 0%/100%); the successor changes at A14, A15, A22, A33, A16 and A17 all match one rewiring; only the relocated activities show large position shifts; and the gap changes (A22→A23 from 2 to 3 events, A33→A18 from 3 to 2) are exactly what placing a two-activity block versus a single-choice activity between those anchors predicts. The 26 qualifying items are many times the fewer than one expected for an unchanged process, so the pattern as a whole is not a sampling artefact. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, DIR001, DIR002]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a single exchange of the two segments from two independent relocations that produce the same net order. In addition, no item covers the outgoing transitions of A18 or the direct relation between A18 and A22, so the wiring of the span between them (relative positions about 0.40 to 0.60) is inferred from the reversed relations and positions rather than observed directly; position and gap indicators use event order, not clock time, but the placement claim here rests on the relational and successor evidence. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, POS005, POS006]
